commands.name: Get-Help
commands.definition: Explains a PowerShell command and its parameters.
commands.expected: Help examples appear; installed help may be limited.
commands.parts: Get-Service names the command; -Examples asks for examples.
commands.usage: Use when you know a command’s name but not its options.

commands.name: Get-Command
commands.definition: Finds commands available in this shell.
commands.expected: Commands whose names contain Service.
commands.parts: * is a wildcard: it matches any text.
commands.usage: Check whether a cmdlet or required module is available.

commands.name: Get-Location
commands.definition: Shows the folder your shell is currently using.
commands.expected: A Path value such as C:\Users\YourName.
commands.parts: Relative paths such as .\notes.txt start from this folder.
commands.usage: Check your location before using a relative filename.

commands.name: Set-Location
commands.definition: Changes the shell’s current folder.
commands.expected: No usual output; Get-Location now shows the parent folder.
commands.parts: .. means the parent directory. It does not move files.
commands.usage: Move one folder up; type Set-Location $HOME to return home.

commands.name: Get-ChildItem
commands.definition: Lists files and folders.
commands.expected: A listing including hidden items you are allowed to see.
commands.parts: -Force includes hidden items; it does not grant extra permissions.
commands.usage: Look for a missing or hidden practice file.

commands.name: New-Item
commands.definition: Creates a named file or folder.
commands.expected: A new CloudSeam-Practice folder, or an already-exists message.
commands.parts: -ItemType Directory means folder; .\ starts at your current folder.
commands.usage: Create a dedicated scratch folder. If it exists, reuse it rather than adding -Force.

commands.name: Get-Content
commands.definition: Reads a text file.
commands.expected: Text from win.ini; an empty file can produce no text.
commands.parts: $env:WINDIR is the Windows directory; quotes keep the path together.
commands.usage: Inspect text without opening an editor. If the file is absent, record that result; do not create system files.

commands.name: Copy-Item
commands.definition: Copies a file or folder to another location.
commands.expected: Confirmation and a copied file; successful copies usually print nothing.
commands.parts: -LiteralPath treats the path literally; -Confirm asks before the copy.
commands.usage: First create your own dummy readme.txt in CloudSeam-Practice. Use only scratch files; an existing destination can be replaced.

commands.name: Get-FileHash
commands.definition: Calculates a file’s checksum for comparison.
commands.expected: A SHA256 hash and the file path.
commands.parts: -Algorithm SHA256 selects the hash method.
commands.usage: Compare a download with its publisher’s hash. A hash alone is not a signature.

commands.name: whoami
commands.definition: Shows the account running the command.
commands.expected: An identity such as lab\learner or dc01\administrator.
commands.parts: A domain\user value identifies the current security context.
commands.usage: Confirm which account is running a task before troubleshooting permissions.

commands.name: hostname
commands.definition: Shows the computer’s short host name.
commands.expected: A short name such as DC01.
commands.parts: DC01 is not an FQDN; dc01.lab.example.test includes the DNS domain.
commands.usage: Confirm you are in the intended VM, not the physical host.

commands.name: ipconfig
commands.definition: Shows Windows network-adapter configuration.
commands.expected: Adapter addresses, masks, DNS settings and other details.
commands.parts: /all adds detailed configuration; it does not change addresses.
commands.usage: Compare the VM’s IP and DNS with the lab plan.

commands.name: ping
commands.definition: Sends ICMP requests to test whether a host replies.
commands.expected: Replies or a specific name-resolution/timeout error.
commands.parts: The FQDN is an example: replace it with your configured target.
commands.usage: Test basic reachability. A blocked ping does not prove the application or computer is down.

commands.name: tracert
commands.definition: Shows responding hops along a route.
commands.expected: Responding hops or timeout markers.
commands.parts: -d skips reverse-name lookups; the IP is the example DC01 address.
commands.usage: Check a route to your own approved lab target; some devices do not answer probes.

commands.name: nslookup
commands.definition: Asks a DNS server to resolve a name.
commands.expected: The DNS server used and an answer or lookup error.
commands.parts: Use the real FQDN from your lab. This does not create DNS records.
commands.usage: Check DNS separately from ping.

commands.name: Test-NetConnection
commands.definition: Tests connectivity, including a chosen TCP port.
commands.expected: TcpTestSucceeded is True or False, plus connection details.
commands.parts: -Port 389 tests the LDAP TCP listener, not every AD feature.
commands.usage: Use your actual DC FQDN. A successful TCP check does not prove authentication or application health.

commands.name: Resolve-DnsName
commands.definition: Looks up DNS records by name and type.
commands.expected: IPv4 A-record results or a specific DNS error.
commands.parts: -Type A requests an IPv4 address record.
commands.usage: Replace the example FQDN with an existing lab DNS record.

commands.name: Get-NetIPConfiguration
commands.definition: Shows IP, gateway and DNS information for interfaces.
commands.expected: Interface details and current IP settings.
commands.parts: InterfaceAlias helps identify which adapter you are inspecting.
commands.usage: Read configuration before changing the intended VM adapter.

commands.name: Get-Service
commands.definition: Shows installed services and their current state.
commands.expected: The Windows Time service and Running or Stopped state.
commands.parts: -Name uses the service name, not its longer display label.
commands.usage: Inspect a service before considering any restart. This command does not start it.

commands.name: Get-Process
commands.definition: Lists processes currently running on this computer.
commands.expected: Five processes sorted by accumulated CPU time.
commands.parts: | passes objects onward; CPU is cumulative time, not current CPU percentage.
commands.usage: Find processes worth investigating without stopping them.

commands.name: Get-WinEvent
commands.definition: Reads Windows Event Log entries.
commands.expected: The five newest available System events, if you have access.
commands.parts: -LogName selects a log; -MaxEvents limits returned entries.
commands.usage: Start with a small event sample. Some logs require elevation or delegated access.

commands.name: Get-WindowsFeature
commands.definition: Shows Windows Server roles and features.
commands.expected: Install State for AD DS and DNS.
commands.parts: A comma separates the two feature names. Installed roles do not prove DC promotion.
commands.usage: Run inside Windows Server with the ServerManager module; this cmdlet does not install roles.

commands.name: Get-ADDomainController
commands.definition: Reads information about a domain controller.
commands.expected: The selected controller’s host name, domain and other properties.
commands.parts: -Identity names the existing DC; HostName may show its FQDN.
commands.usage: Requires the ActiveDirectory module, working domain connectivity and an authorized account.
commands.effect: Read-only; AD module and domain access

commands.name: dcdiag
commands.definition: Runs domain-controller diagnostic tests.
commands.expected: Detailed DNS-test findings; review individual failures.
commands.parts: /test:DNS selects DNS diagnostics; /v adds detail. No /fix is used.
commands.usage: Run elevated on your disposable DC with AD DS tools installed. A single passing test is not proof of complete AD health.

commands.name: Get-PSDrive
commands.definition: Lists drives exposed by PowerShell providers.
commands.expected: File-system drives and available space where reported.
commands.parts: -PSProvider FileSystem excludes providers such as Registry.
commands.usage: Check disk space and drive visibility before writing a file.

commands.name: pwd
commands.definition: Prints the full current working directory.
commands.expected: A path such as /home/learner.
commands.parts: pwd means print working directory.
commands.usage: Use before a command that contains a relative path.

commands.name: ls
commands.definition: Lists directory contents.
commands.expected: A detailed listing, including dotfiles.
commands.parts: -l is long format; -a includes hidden entries; -h uses readable sizes.
commands.usage: Inspect names and permissions; hidden files usually begin with a dot.

commands.name: cd
commands.definition: Changes the current shell directory.
commands.expected: Usually no output; pwd now prints /.
commands.parts: / is the filesystem root directory, not the root user.
commands.usage: Return home with cd ~. Your user can stay learner even when the current folder is /.

commands.name: mkdir
commands.definition: Creates directories.
commands.expected: The practice folder exists; success usually prints nothing.
commands.parts: ~ is your home; -p also creates missing parent folders.
commands.usage: Make a dedicated scratch folder before file exercises.

commands.name: touch
commands.definition: Creates an empty file or updates an existing file’s timestamps.
commands.expected: The file exists; an existing file keeps its contents.
commands.parts: The parent folder must already exist.
commands.usage: Create the scratch folder with mkdir first; use only your own practice file.
commands.effect: Creates a file or changes its timestamps

commands.name: cat
commands.definition: Writes a file’s contents to the terminal.
commands.expected: The installed distribution’s name and version fields.
commands.parts: /etc/os-release is an absolute path, starting at /.
commands.usage: Confirm the actual Linux version before following version-specific instructions.

commands.name: less
commands.definition: Opens text in a scrollable terminal viewer.
commands.expected: A text viewer; press q to return to the prompt.
commands.parts: Arrow keys scroll; / starts a search; q quits the viewer.
commands.usage: Read a long file without opening an editor. Requires less to be installed.

commands.name: cp
commands.definition: Copies a file to another path.
commands.expected: A copied file; asks before overwriting an existing destination.
commands.parts: -i prompts before replacement. Read the source and destination order carefully.
commands.usage: Create the scratch folder and dummy readme.txt first. Answer n if an existing destination should be kept.

commands.name: grep
commands.definition: Prints text lines matching a pattern.
commands.expected: Matching VERSION lines with line numbers.
commands.parts: -n adds line numbers; matching is case-sensitive by default.
commands.usage: Find a setting in text without changing the file.

commands.name: find
commands.definition: Searches a directory tree for matching entries.
commands.expected: Files found within the practice folder’s depth limit.
commands.parts: -maxdepth 2 limits traversal; -type f selects regular files.
commands.usage: Create the scratch folder first. No output can simply mean no files matched.

commands.name: whoami
commands.definition: Prints the effective current user name.
commands.expected: Your effective account name, such as learner.
commands.parts: The result describes who the command is running as.
commands.usage: Confirm identity before interpreting a permission problem.

commands.name: id
commands.definition: Shows a user’s numeric IDs and group memberships.
commands.expected: uid, gid and supplementary groups.
commands.parts: uid identifies the user; gid identifies a group.
commands.usage: Check group membership; changed memberships may require a fresh sign-in.

commands.name: hostnamectl
commands.definition: Shows host identity and system information on systemd systems.
commands.expected: The configured host name and system details.
commands.parts: status reads information; it does not rename the server.
commands.usage: A short hostname and a DNS FQDN are different. Do not assume this output proves DNS registration.

commands.name: ip
commands.definition: Inspects Linux network interfaces, addresses and routes.
commands.expected: A compact address listing for interfaces.
commands.parts: -br means brief; address selects interface addresses.
commands.usage: Compare the intended interface with your private lab address plan.

commands.name: ss
commands.definition: Shows socket and listening-port information.
commands.expected: Listening TCP sockets with numeric ports.
commands.parts: -l means listening; -t means TCP; -n skips name resolution.
commands.usage: Check for a listener before blaming the firewall. A listener alone does not prove application health.

commands.name: ping
commands.definition: Sends ICMP requests to test for replies.
commands.expected: Four local loopback probes and a summary.
commands.parts: -c 4 limits the count. 127.0.0.1 is this machine, not another VM.
commands.usage: Start locally, then use your actual approved lab target. A missing reply is not a complete diagnosis.

commands.name: df
commands.definition: Shows disk space used and available on mounted filesystems.
commands.expected: Used and available space for the filesystem containing /.
commands.parts: -h uses readable sizes; / selects the root filesystem.
commands.usage: Check which filesystem is full before looking for large folders.

commands.name: du
commands.definition: Estimates disk space used by files and directories.
commands.expected: A total for the scratch folder.
commands.parts: -s gives a summary; -h uses readable sizes.
commands.usage: Create the scratch folder first. du measures files; df reports filesystem usage, so their totals can differ.

commands.name: free
commands.definition: Shows memory and swap usage.
commands.expected: RAM and swap totals in readable units.
commands.parts: Look at available memory as well as free; Linux uses RAM for caches.
commands.usage: Get a first memory snapshot before investigating specific processes.

commands.name: ps
commands.definition: Shows a snapshot of processes.
commands.expected: A full-format process list.
commands.parts: -e includes all processes; -f adds full details such as command and parent ID.
commands.usage: Identify a process before considering any stop or restart.

commands.name: systemctl
commands.definition: Inspects and manages systemd units.
commands.expected: The sshd unit’s state and recent status details, or unit-not-found.
commands.parts: status reads; --no-pager prevents an interactive viewer.
commands.usage: This example only reads. sshd must be installed; active does not prove a remote login will work.

commands.name: journalctl
commands.definition: Reads the systemd journal.
commands.expected: Up to 20 accessible journal entries for sshd.
commands.parts: sudo uses authorized elevation; -u selects a unit; -n limits entries.
commands.usage: Use an account with approved sudo access. Passwords are entered locally and are not echoed. Empty output can mean no matching retained entries.
commands.effect: Read-only; sudo access for full journal

commands.name: dnf
commands.definition: Queries and manages RPM-based distribution packages.
commands.expected: The installed openssl package, or no matching installed package.
commands.parts: list --installed reads installed-package information; this is not an install command.
commands.usage: For RHEL/AlmaLinux with DNF; package names and available tools vary by distribution.
commands.effect: Reads package information; may refresh metadata

commands.name: rpm
commands.definition: Queries RPM package information and manages RPM files.
commands.expected: The installed package version or a not-installed message.
commands.parts: -q queries the local RPM database.
commands.usage: Check the installed package separately from whether its program is running.

commands.name: chmod
commands.definition: Changes permission bits on a file or directory.
commands.expected: Usually no output; ls -l now begins with -rw------- for that regular file.
commands.parts: 600 gives the owner read/write and removes group/other access bits.
commands.usage: Use only your own dummy file. This changes mode bits; it is not a complete ACL or SELinux access check.

commands.name: man
commands.definition: Opens an installed command manual.
commands.expected: The ls manual, if installed; q returns to the prompt.
commands.parts: The word after man is the manual topic.
commands.usage: Minimal installations may lack manual pages; use the linked official reference if so.
